strengths: Addresses a timely and underexplored question: whether feed-forward 3D foundation models (VGGT) internalize principled geometric reasoning (epipolar geometry, correspondence) versus relying purely on learned appearance priors, filling a genuine gap relative to prior interpretability work that has focused mostly on LLMs and discriminative vision models.

Methodologically thorough multi-pronged analysis: linear probing across layers, QK attention-space correspondence analysis, and causal attention-knockout interventions, with the supplementary providing increasingly localized interventions (whole-map -> patch-level -> individual correspondence) that meaningfully strengthen the causal claims beyond simple correlation.

Well-designed controlled synthetic benchmark with full ground truth (camera parameters, correspondences, fundamental/essential matrices) enabling precise, unconfounded probing that would be hard to obtain from real-world data.

The identification of a consistent transition point (~layer 10-14) where correspondence matching and epipolar-geometry decodability emerge together, corroborated by both Sampson error and rank-2 singular-value analysis, provides a coherent and internally consistent story.

Extensive robustness comparisons (occlusion, lighting/color, symmetry/repetition, focal length) against both classical (SIFT+RANSAC) and learned (SuperGlue+RANSAC) baselines give useful practical insight into VGGT's data-driven robustness and its failure modes (e.g., asymmetric lighting, shadow removal), including an interesting and candidly discussed 'hallucination' phenomenon under occlusion.

Authors are appropriately forthright about limitations (synthetic-only data, non-local interventions, confounds with classical baselines on texture-less renders, inability to prove correspondence heads are the sole cause of epipolar geometry).
weaknesses: All experiments are conducted on a small, fairly simple synthetic ShapeNet-rendered dataset (as few as 40 object instances across 10 categories); it remains unclear how well the mechanistic findings (layer localization, causal head roles) transfer to VGGT's behavior on complex real-world scenes with clutter, texture, and diverse camera trajectories it was actually trained on.

The study examines a single model (VGGT) only; no comparison to other feed-forward 3D reconstruction architectures (e.g., DUSt3R, MASt3R, VGGSfM) is provided, which would help establish whether the observed geometric emergence is a general property of this model family or specific to VGGT's particular training/architecture.

Probing is restricted to the camera token at each layer; patch/local tokens, which likely carry substantial correspondence and geometric information, are not probed, potentially underestimating or mischaracterizing where and how geometric information is distributed in the representation.

The causal interpretation remains only partially resolved: even with progressively localized attention knockouts, the paper cannot rule out that the implicated heads perform functions beyond correspondence matching that also contribute to the observed degradation (acknowledged by the authors themselves).

Comparisons with SIFT+RANSAC and SuperGlue+RANSAC baselines are potentially confounded by known weaknesses of these classical/local methods on synthetic, texture-poor renders, limiting the strength of the robustness claims about VGGT's superiority (also acknowledged as a limitation, but not mitigated by e.g. additional feature detectors or tuned classical pipelines).

Reported results are largely based on medians/aggregate statistics without confidence intervals or variance across scenes/objects, making it harder to judge the statistical robustness of the layer-wise transitions and intervention effects.
No explicit statement on code/dataset release for reproducibility is provided in the main text, which would be important given the custom synthetic dataset and analysis pipeline.

strengths: Addresses a timely and important question—whether feed-forward 3D reconstruction models (DUSt3R, VGGT, DA3) internalize classical geometric principles (epipolar geometry, correspondence) or rely mainly on learned priors—which is valuable to the community given the rapid adoption of these foundation models.

Combines correlational evidence (layer-wise probing for the fundamental matrix, rank-2/singular-value checks, attention-map correspondence analysis, feature-similarity analysis) with causal evidence (attention-knockout interventions at four levels of locality), which is methodologically stronger than probing alone and helps substantiate the causal claim that correspondence-forming attention heads support the encoded epipolar geometry.

Broad empirical scope: three real-world datasets (DTU, ETH3D, MipNeRF360) plus a carefully constructed, fully-controlled synthetic ShapeNet dataset with ground-truth camera geometry, correspondences, and fundamental/essential matrices, enabling systematic manipulation of viewpoint, focal length, symmetry/repetition, and occlusion.

Findings are largely consistent across models and datasets (middle-layer emergence for VGGT/DA3, early-layer emergence for DUSt3R), lending credibility to the conclusions, and the extensive appendix (probe ablations, multi-view/triplet consistency, semantic correspondence, model-size sweeps for DA3, additional interventions) supports robustness of the central claims.

The robustness/learned-priors study (occlusion 'hallucination' behavior, lighting/color robustness, symmetric/repetitive scene failure, focal-length robustness) yields practically relevant insights, e.g., that VGGT partially reconstructs correspondences in occluded regions via learned priors rather than leaving them unmatched, which has direct implications for reliability in downstream 3D applications.
weaknesses: The contribution is primarily an empirical/interpretability analysis rather than a new algorithm, dataset, or theory; while this is a legitimate and useful contribution type, the insights delivered (models form correspondence-like attention structure that supports approximate epipolar geometry) are largely confirmatory of what one would expect rather than surprising, somewhat limiting novelty.

For DUSt3R, a large fraction (72%) of whole-head/image-map interventions produce invalid camera-pose predictions and are excluded from analysis, which weakens the strength and completeness of the causal claims for this model and suggests the intervention protocol may not transfer cleanly across architectures.

Baselines for the classical/learned-prior comparison (SIFT+8-point, SuperGlue) are relatively dated; more recent detector-free matchers (e.g., LoFTR, RoMa) mentioned in related work are not used in the comparative robustness experiments, which would have made the 'learned priors vs. classical pipelines' claims more convincing.

Many quantitative results (bar charts, heatmaps) are reported without error bars, statistical significance testing, or larger-scale ablations, making it harder to judge the reliability of some fine-grained trends (e.g., subtle inter-model differences in emergence layer, or the qualitative-only rank-2/singular-value evidence).

The synthetic dataset, while well controlled, consists of relatively simple, clean object-centric scenes; the occlusion/ambiguity findings, though interesting, are not validated on more complex real scenes with actual downstream reconstruction-quality metrics (only correspondence/Sampson-error proxies are used).

Several explanatory claims about architectural differences (e.g., why DA3 exhibits particular layer patterns, why VGGT's semantic-to-geometric transition occurs) are speculative ("we believe", "may stem from") without direct verification.
No explicit statement on code/data release is evident, which affects reproducibility of the fairly complex multi-model, multi-dataset analysis pipeline.

strengths: Addresses a timely and important question for the field: whether feed-forward 3D reconstruction foundation models (DUSt3R, VGGT, Depth Anything 3) internalize classical geometric principles (epipolar geometry) or primarily rely on learned data priors.

Employs a multi-pronged methodology combining linear/MLP probing of intermediate representations, attention-pattern analysis for correspondence matching, and causal attention-knockout interventions at multiple localities (whole head, image map, block, patch), which together build a convincing case rather than relying on a single diagnostic.

Introduces a well-designed, fully-controlled synthetic ShapeNet-based dataset with exact ground-truth camera poses, correspondences, and fundamental/essential matrices, enabling precise manipulation of viewpoint, focal length, symmetry, and occlusion that would be impossible with real data alone.

Extensive experimental coverage: three real-world datasets (DTU, ETH3D, MipNeRF360) plus SPair71k for semantic correspondence, three model architectures, multiple DA3 model sizes, two-view and three-view settings, and multiple probe designs (linear vs. MLP, early-stopping ablations) that support the robustness of the reported trends.

The causal attention-knockout experiments (Sec. 4.3, App. D) go beyond correlational probing evidence and provide a genuine causal link between correspondence-encoding attention heads and the emergent epipolar-geometry representation.

The learned-prior robustness study (Sec. 5) offers nuanced, non-trivial findings, e.g., VGGT partially 'hallucinates' correspondences under occlusion (partially beneficial but sometimes undesirable) and outperforms classical/learned pipelines under lighting, focal-length, and moderate symmetry perturbations while still failing under fully symmetric/ambiguous configurations, mirroring the fundamental limits of multi-view geometry.

The paper is transparent about failure cases and limitations of its own causal claims (e.g., acknowledging that attention heads may encode more than correspondence, and that DUSt3R's cross-attention interventions frequently produce invalid poses), which strengthens the credibility of the analysis.
weaknesses: The learned-prior robustness study (Section 5) is conducted almost exclusively on VGGT; DUSt3R and DA3 are not evaluated under the same occlusion/lighting/symmetry perturbations, which limits how broadly the 'reliance on learned priors' conclusion can be generalized across all three studied architectures.

The causal interventions, while informative, are still somewhat coarse (zeroing full heads or spatial neighborhoods) and the authors themselves note this does not conclusively isolate correspondence matching as the sole mechanism responsible for epipolar-geometry encoding — some claims remain partially correlational despite the causal framing.

The custom ShapeNet dataset, though useful for control, consists of single objects against relatively simple backgrounds/rendered scenes, which may not fully capture the complexity (clutter, dynamic elements, real-world lighting/texture variation) present in the real deployment settings these models target; generalizability of fine-grained layer-wise findings to more complex real scenes is only partially validated via the real-world datasets.

The overall narrative conclusions (models partly learn geometry, but also rely heavily on data priors that aid in-distribution robustness yet can cause hallucination) are reasonable but largely confirmatory of prior intuitions in the field rather than delivering a strong surprising or actionable mechanistic insight (e.g., no concrete recommendation for architecture/training changes that would follow from the findings).

Dense multi-panel figures (e.g., Figs. 2, 3, 12, 16, 18) are visually cluttered and their axis labels are difficult to parse at the given resolution, which may hinder reproducibility/clarity for readers not consulting the supplementary material closely.

As an interpretability/analysis contribution (no new algorithm proposed), the paper's significance rests on the depth and reliability of its mechanistic claims; while the evidence is reasonably thorough, some conclusions (e.g., 'geometric phase transition,' 'inpainting-like' behavior) are somewhat speculative interpretations of the observed patterns rather than fully validated mechanisms.
